content:
Hi all — first post here. We're a small group formalizing parts of the
NIST SP 800-90B entropy-source standard. Our first sorry-free proof
(produced via Harmonic's Aristotle) formalizes the §6.3.1 Most Common
Value (MCV) min-entropy estimator's conservativeness property.

The deterministic core — the −log₂ antitone-on-positives argument
that turns "p̂_max upper-bound ≥ p_max ⇒ MCV estimate ≤ true min-entropy"
— is fully proved against current Mathlib. The probabilistic wrapper
currently takes the normal-approximation event probability as a
hypothesis rather than deriving it from first principles, because we
didn't find a packaged standard normal CDF Φ and its inverse Φ⁻¹
in mathlib in a form we could use directly. MeasureTheory.gaussianReal
looks like the right neighborhood for the density, but we didn't see
a CDF on top of it.

Two questions, in priority order:

  1. **Is there ongoing or planned work on Φ / Φ⁻¹ in mathlib that we
    should track?** Happy to wait on someone else's slice if it's in the
    pipeline, since this isn't our area of deep expertise.

  2. If not, would a contribution be welcome? We'd plan it small —
    start with whatever piece is missing (density properties? CDF via
    integral? inverse via continuous-monotonic argument?), align on
    naming and proof style here on Zulip before any PR, and not commit
    to the whole stack at once.

We're realistic about effort: small group with limited Lean seniority,
so any contribution would be staged across weeks-to-months rather than
rapid-fire. We'd much rather contribute one well-aligned slice than a
sprawling PR that needs heavy rework.

The proof itself is in our private working tree right now — happy to
share specifics if it would help the conversation, just DM. If there's
an existing thread or issue to redirect us to, that's also a great
answer. Thanks for reading — and for mathlib generally

Hi! Indeed there isn’t much about cdf in mathlib (see this file and dependencies). I am not aware of any work about that, although that does not mean there isn’t. If you want to talk about the inverse of the cdf I’d say you would have to define it for a general docs#StieltjesFunction first. Let me emphasize however that we are seeing many PRs by new contributors that are LLM generated, and for reasons explained for instance in #mathlib4 > What to do with "slop" PRs @ 💬 these are unlikely to be reviewed and likely to be closed, see the contribution guidelines about AI for more details.
I notice you didn’t really respond to the point about AI PRs and AI policy from @Etienne Marion , did you happen to read that part of his message ?

Nice to meet you Yan,

didn't find it necessary to respond to — but here is my response — yes it was acknowledged! @Etienne Marion

any relevant thoughts on the discussion above @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 ? That would be genuinely appreciated

cheers

Anand Nambakam said:

Nice to meet you Yan,

didn't find it necessary to respond to — but here is my response — yes it was acknowledged! Etienne Marion

any relevant thoughts on the discussion above Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 ? That would be genuinely appreciated

cheers

I guess I can say the same to you, "didn't find it necessary to respond to" the discussion, if it can be that simple.

It depends though, did an LLM write that discussion? You will find more traction if it doesn't appear as such, because people are less willing to middleman a discussion between you and the model.

I had a very brief look at that code, and there is not much for me to say to you except that as it stands these are results more about Stieltjes/reals and is not connected to CDFs directly at this stage. So you would really be framing this as another question.

These should also be stated in more generality than just this context then if possible (and in this case for some of them, that seems very applicable), which may then be applied in a specific setting, as Mathlib aims for full generality. You should make sure these aren't easily implied by more general results, but I don't have the time to trawl and determine exactly how it meshes.

All in all though , even if it was the correct generality, relevant, and not redundant, the code would need a lot of work for Mathlib. It is dirty and thankless work to refactor such AI code, so this effort will have to come from you.

And further it is often thankless to mentor such a PR when the feedback is fed into the LLM, rather than feeling rewarded from imbuing skills to a human, so you may also have to do a lot of solo learning and figure it out with less guidance.

I recommend not to think about Mathlib for now (unless you plan to get your hand dirty and learn a good amount of the language yourself), you said you did not feel the need to respond to Etienne, but if you did read it, you should know LLM code is simply not up to Mathlib par without human guidance.

I strongly encourage you to make your messages a lot less verbose , and not to use LLM for them, if you do.

You are relying on altruism when you want people to volunteer their time and read these and help you, so its nice if you make it easier for us too.
Fair enough — we'll keep it in our own tree for now; happy for someone to pick it up later if it's useful. Thanks both for the time

Anand Nambakam said:

Fair enough — we'll keep it in our own tree for now; happy for someone to pick it up later if it's useful. Thanks both for the time

If you like , you can look into projects like #GibbsMeasure and such, and how they have this feature called upstreaming dashboard.

Even humans struggle writing Mathlib level code , so it’s not uncommon for human code to be in your own repo and then another version is prepared for Mathlib , gradually putting results in over time.

It’s just as things stand , that second part can’t be done with just AI, regardless if the original poor quality code was human or AI!

So I don’t mean to discourage you too hard , I actually would rather encourage you to try this overall :smiling_face: ! Just needs some manual work.

Or you can just wait and maybe AI will be good enough soon :saluting_face:

Moderation note: two messages that looked LLM-generated were deleted in this thread.

Using LLMs to write comments on zulip is against this site's policy (and erodes the human element this project is about). It will lead to your comment being deleted and you being suspended. Write comments by hand, please.
